description: Contact-mechanics theory database anchoring Tabor regime classification, plastic contact area, and volume-conservation constraints used in scripts/plastic_coverage.py (Physics mode) and scripts/network_conductivity.py.

our_dem_method.approach: effective-modulus (E_eff) calibration — standard DEM convention to absorb plastic + rate-dependent + cohesive contact effects into a single reduced stiffness (Cundall-Strack 1979; Thornton 1997).
our_dem_method.calibration_target: porosity matched to experimental pellet at target compaction pressure
our_dem_method.calibration_method: linear regression sweeping E_eff and picking the value that minimises porosity residual
rationale: Real LPSCl undergoes plastic flow above yield (σ_y ≈ 0.30 GPa, Sakuda 2013) — DEM with E_real would hit elastic overlap only, missing real densification.
Softening E_eff allows DEM to reach the same equilibrium porosity at the same applied pressure P, with larger overlap δ_sim that effectively represents the post-plastic-flow contact state.

implications_for_analysis.A_liggghts_inflation: A = π·R·δ inflated by the same factor as δ (linear in δ for small-overlap Hertz) — already behaves as a plastic contact area proxy
implications_for_analysis.hertzian_mode_interpretation: Use LIGGGHTS contact_area directly. δ_sim is E_eff-calibrated → A_liggghts is the internally-consistent plastic proxy.
implications_for_analysis.physics_mode_interpretation: Recomputes F_real from δ_sim with E_real (not E_eff) and applies Tabor A = F/H. When δ_sim is already inflated by E_eff calibration, this adds a second plastic correction — treat as UPPER BOUND, not independent prediction. Lower-bounded by A_liggghts so never goes below Hertzian.
implications_for_analysis.recommended_defense_framing: Primary: Hertzian (E_eff-calibrated DEM-native). Sensitivity: Physics (E_real + Tabor) as the upper bound of the σ band.

why_delta_over_R_is_the_only_indicator.central_claim: δ/R* is the ONLY plastic-deformation indicator that survives E_eff calibration unchanged — every other DEM observable (force, contact pressure, energy) is scaled by E_eff and cannot be used at face value.

delta_overlap.reason: pure kinematic quantity from particle centers and radii

delta_over_R.reason: dimensionless ratio of two geometric observables — primary plastic proxy

F_contact.reason: F_sim = (4/3) E_eff √R δ^1.5  — scaled by E_eff → ~18× smaller than real F

contact_energy.reason: integral of F·dδ → inherits F pollution

contact_area_LIGGGHTS.reason: A = π·R·δ_sim → inflated via δ only, not via any E-dependent force; interpretable as post-plastic-flow contact proxy under E_eff framework

causal_chain_from_delta_to_sigma.name: regime_classification
causal_chain_from_delta_to_sigma.logic: Jackson-Green 2005 FEM thresholds (1.5% onset, 4% full plasticity)

causal_chain_from_delta_to_sigma.name: contact_area
causal_chain_from_delta_to_sigma.logic: Hertzian: A = π R δ from LIGGGHTS (E_eff-calibrated) | Physics: A = min(F_real/H, V/h_film, 2πR_min²) with F_real=(4/3)E_real√R·δ^1.5 lower-bounded by A_liggghts

causal_chain_from_delta_to_sigma.name: bulk_resistance
causal_chain_from_delta_to_sigma.logic: Ohmic bulk through each sphere segment

causal_chain_from_delta_to_sigma.name: network_solve
causal_chain_from_delta_to_sigma.logic: Kirchhoff Laplacian L·V=b solved via CG→ILU→spsolve (3-stage)

why_delta_over_R_is_the_only_indicator.why_F_is_never_read_from_DEM: LIGGGHTS outputs F_sim computed with E_eff (= 1.35 GPa here). Using F_sim directly for any plasticity metric would propagate the ~18× E-scaling artifact. Physics mode avoids this by RECOMPUTING F_real = (4/3)·E_real·√R·δ^1.5 from the measured δ_sim using the literature E_real — bypassing the DEM force entirely. The only δ-derived input is geometric, so the Tabor step is force-model-agnostic.
why_delta_over_R_is_the_only_indicator.double_correction_caveat: Even with F_real recomputation, Physics mode uses δ_sim (inflated 6.9× by E_eff calibration) in the F_real formula → F_real ∝ δ^1.5 → F_real ~ 18× the actual real-material value. A_tabor is correspondingly inflated. This is why Physics is labelled an UPPER BOUND and kept above A_liggghts by the lower-bound rule rather than replacing it.
why_delta_over_R_is_the_only_indicator.why_hertzian_is_the_primary_mode: A_liggghts carries the E_eff-calibrated plastic state internally consistent with the simulation that produced it. The porosity-regression calibration (E_eff=1.35 GPa ↔ experimental porosity at target P) is a single-parameter plastic absorption: whatever compaction experiments show, the simulation reproduces → contact areas reflect that state. No external Tabor reconstruction needed for self-consistency.

our_dem_method.method_section_one_liner: DEM simulations use an effective Young's modulus E_eff=1.35 GPa, porosity-calibrated by linear regression against the experimental pellet at target compaction pressure, following the standard DEM convention of absorbing plastic and rate-dependent contact effects into a reduced stiffness (Cundall & Strack 1979; Thornton et al. 2013). Because DEM-reported forces are scaled by E_eff/E_real≈0.056, the only plastic-deformation indicator that remains E-independent is the normalized overlap δ/R*. All regime classification (elastic/transition/plastic via Jackson-Green 2005 thresholds) and contact-area computation therefore rely exclusively on δ/R*. The Hertzian analysis mode uses the LIGGGHTS-reported contact_area=π·R*·δ_sim (self-consistent within the E_eff frame) and serves as the primary estimator. The Physics analysis mode provides a sensitivity upper bound by recomputing F_real=(4/3)·E_real·√R*·δ^1.5 with E_real from literature (Sakuda 2013) and applying Tabor's plastic relation A=F_real/H with volume-conservation and hemisphere caps (lower-bounded by A_liggghts so it never falls below the DEM-native value). Contact radii a=√(A/π) feed Holm-Maxwell spreading resistance R_constr=1/(2σa) at every edge of a Kirchhoff resistor network, solved via a three-stage CG → ILU-preconditioned CG → direct LU fallback for robustness on ill-conditioned bottleneck cases.

model_summary.tabor_number: mu_T = (sigma_y^3 * R / (E_star^2 * F))^(1/6)  — indentation plasticity index. mu_T > 1 → elastic (Hertz), mu_T << 1 → fully plastic (Tabor A = F/H).
model_summary.elastic_limit: dr_yield_onset ≈ 1.5% (delta/R*) — below this Hertz is valid
model_summary.full_plasticity: dr_fully_plastic ≈ 4% (delta/R*) — above this Tabor A = F/H applies with H ≈ 2.8 sigma_y
model_summary.volume_conservation: A_plastic <= V_overlap / h_film_min — material cannot vanish on plastic deformation
model_summary.hemisphere_cap: A_plastic <= 2 pi R_min^2 — lateral spread bounded by smallest particle surface
model_summary.lower_bound_rule: A_plastic >= max(A_elastic_hertz, A_liggghts) — physical contact must exceed pure-elastic prediction and the DEM-reported area (which already accounts for in-sim hooke/hysteresis plasticity)

entries.citation: Cundall, P. A. & Strack, O. D. L. A discrete numerical model for granular assemblies. Géotechnique 29, 47-65 (1979).
key_concepts: original DEM formulation
soft-particle contact with overlap-proportional force
precedent for using reduced effective stiffness to enable tractable timesteps

relevance_to_our_model.E_eff_justification: Founding DEM paper establishes the overlap-based soft-contact formulation; the choice of spring stiffness is a modelling parameter, not a material property — legitimises E_eff calibration approach.

entries.citation: Thornton, C., Cummins, S. J. & Cleary, P. W. An investigation of the comparative behaviour of alternative contact force models during elastic collisions. Powder Technology 233, 30-46 (2013).
key_concepts: comparison of hooke, hertz, hertz-hysteresis contact models
timestep-cost vs physical-fidelity trade-off
effective modulus calibration against experimental observables

relevance_to_our_model.E_eff_calibration_standard: Explicitly treats the effective modulus as a free parameter calibrated against experimental benchmarks (here: porosity at applied pressure). Matches our porosity-regression approach for E_eff = 1.35 GPa.

entries.citation: Potyondy, D. O. & Cundall, P. A. A bonded-particle model for rock. Int. J. Rock Mech. Min. Sci. 41, 1329-1364 (2004).
key_concepts: macro-scale calibration of micro-scale DEM parameters
effective stiffness as target-property fitting parameter

relevance_to_our_model.calibration_philosophy: Supports the linear-regression porosity-target methodology we used to set E_eff = 1.35 GPa — DEM micro-parameters are routinely calibrated from experimental macro-observables.

entries.citation: Tabor, D. The Hardness of Metals. Oxford University Press, 1951.
key_concepts: hardness-yield relation H ≈ 2.8 sigma_y
plastic indentation area A_plastic = F / H
strain geometric representation

relevance_to_our_model.plastic_coverage.py:H_REAL_SE: H = 2.8 sigma_y anchor; LPSCl sigma_y ≈ 0.30 GPa → H ≈ 0.85 GPa
relevance_to_our_model.physics_mode_A_tabor: A = F_real / H used as primary plastic-area estimate

equations_provided: H = 2.8 * sigma_y  (Tabor's relation, spherical indenter, work-hardened metals)
A_plastic = F / H  (pure plastic regime, Tabor's plastic indentation)

entries.citation: Johnson, K. L. Contact Mechanics. Cambridge University Press, 1985.
key_concepts: Hertz theory for elastic spherical contact
elastoplastic transition
reduced modulus E_star definition
reduced radius R_star definition

relevance_to_our_model.plastic_coverage.py:F_real: F = (4/3) E_star sqrt(R_star) delta^(3/2)  (Hertz point-contact force) — used to reconstruct 'real' force from sim overlap when E_eff differs from E_real
relevance_to_our_model.A_elastic: A_hertz = pi R_star delta  (small-overlap geometric area)

equations_provided: A_hertz = pi a_hertz^2 ≈ pi R_star delta  (small delta)

relevance_to_our_model.tabor_number_definition: Original derivation of mu_T = (E_star a / sigma_y R)^{-1}  ↔  equivalent form mu_T = (sigma_y^3 R / E_star^2 F)^(1/6) via Hertz substitution

equations_provided: Plasticity index: (E_star/sigma_y) * (a/R)  (critical value ≈ 2.8 for onset of full plasticity)
Regime map: elastic when (E_star a / sigma_y R) < 1.1, plastic when > 2.8

relevance_to_our_model.dissimilar_materials: Justifies using E_star (not pure E) for NCM-LPSCl dissimilar contact

E_STAR_AM_SE_REAL_GPa.derivation: 1/E* = (1-nu_AM^2)/E_AM + (1-nu_SE^2)/E_SE with E_AM=140 GPa (NCM), E_SE=24 GPa (LPSCl); ≈ 20 GPa

H_REAL_SE_GPa.derivation: Tabor H = 2.8 sigma_y with sigma_y_LPSCl ≈ 0.30 GPa (Sakuda 2013 indentation)

H_FILM_MIN_nm.derivation: Minimum plastic film thickness characteristic of sulfide glass flow (Sakuda empirical observation of ~5 nm residual interface)

DR_YIELD_ONSET.derivation: delta/R* at onset of plastic yielding — Jackson-Green FEM boundary

DR_FULLY_PLASTIC.derivation: delta/R* above which Tabor A = F/H saturates
